Left Rotate Array by k number (optimal) class Solution { public void leftRotate(int[] nums, int k) { int n = nums.length; k = k % n; reverse(nums, 0, k - 1); reverse(nums, k, n - 1); reverse(nums, 0, n - 1); } public void reverse(int[] nums, int start, int end) { while (start < end) { int temp = nums[start]; nums[start] = nums[end]; nums[end] = temp; start++; end--; } } }

IoT Protocols According to your PPT, IoT protocols are communication protocols that allow IoT devices to communicate with each other and with IoT infrastructure. They are organized into four main layers: Link Layer, Network/Internet Layer, Transport Layer, and Application Layer. 1. Link Layer The Link Layer determines how data is physically sent over the network medium, such as a cable, copper wire, or radio wave. It also determines how packets are coded and signaled by the hardware. Important Link Layer protocols a) IEEE 802.3 – Ethernet A collection of wired Ethernet standards. Uses media such as coaxial cable, twisted-pair wire, and optical fiber. Provides wired network communication. b) IEEE 802.11 – Wi-Fi Wireless LAN communication standard. Different versions operate at different frequency bands. c) IEEE 802.16 – WiMAX Wireless broadband standard. Provides relatively long-range wireless communication. d) IEEE 802.15.4 – LR-WPAN Means Low-Rate Wireless Personal Area Network. Forms the basis for technologies such as Zigbee. Designed for low-cost, low-speed, power-constrained devices. e) 2G / 3G / 4G Mobile communication standards used for cellular connectivity. Include GSM/CDMA, UMTS/CDMA2000 and LTE. 2. Network / Internet Layer The Network layer is responsible for sending IP datagrams from the source network to the destination network. Its main functions are: Host addressing Packet routing Identifying source and destination Sending packets across multiple networks The PPT lists IPv4, IPv6 and 6LoWPAN at this layer. a) IPv4 Uses a 32-bit address. Provides approximately 2³² addresses. It has been widely deployed. Due to the increasing number of Internet-connected devices, IPv6 was introduced as its successor. b) IPv6 Successor to IPv4. Uses a 128-bit address. Provides approximately 2¹²⁸ addresses. This large address space is useful for the huge number of IoT devices. c) 6LoWPAN IPv6 over Low-Power Wireless Personal Area Networks Brings IP/IPv6 communication to low-power devices. Designed for devices with limited processing capabilities. Works with low-power wireless networks. 3. Transport Layer The Transport Layer provides end-to-end message transfer independently of the underlying network. Its functions include: Error control Segmentation Flow control Congestion control The two important protocols are TCP and UDP. a) TCP – Transmission Control Protocol TCP is: Connection-oriented Stateful Provides reliable transmission Ensures packets are delivered in order Can detect errors Can retransmit lost packets Provides flow control TCP is commonly used with protocols such as HTTP/HTTPS. Easy example: If an IoT device needs reliable delivery of data, TCP can be used. b) UDP – User

Easy example: If an IoT device needs reliable delivery of data, TCP can be used. b) UDP – User Datagram Protocol UDP is: Connectionless Stateless Has low communication overhead Useful for time-sensitive applications Does not guarantee delivery Does not guarantee ordering Does not eliminate duplicate messages. Easy example: For an IoT application where speed is more important than guaranteed delivery, UDP can be useful. 4. Application Layer The Application Layer defines how an application communicates with the lower-layer protocols to send and receive data. Your PPT includes: HTTP CoAP WebSocket MQTT XMPP DDS AMQP Let's understand each one. a) HTTP – Hypertext Transfer Protocol HTTP is an application-layer protocol and forms the foundation of the World Wide Web. It follows the request-response model: Client ───── Request ─────> Server Client <──── Response ───── Server It includes methods such as: GET PUT POST DELETE HEAD HTTP is stateless, meaning each request is treated independently. b) CoAP – Constrained Application Protocol CoAP is designed for: Machine-to-machine (M2M) applications Constrained devices Constrained networks It is similar to HTTP and follows the request-response model, but it runs over UDP instead of TCP. It supports methods such as: GET PUT DELETE Easy point: 👉 CoAP = HTTP-like protocol for constrained IoT devices c) WebSocket WebSocket provides full-duplex communication between a client and server. It: Uses TCP Keeps the connection open Allows messages to flow in both directions Supports continuous communication Both client and server can send messages after the connection is established. M2M vs IoT According to your PPT, M2M and IoT differ mainly in their communication scope, protocols, type of devices, and applications/data handling. Focus specifically on the 3 asked points 1. Communication Scope M2M: Communication is mainly between machines in an M2M area network. To communicate with remote M2M networks, an M2M gateway is used. IoT: Communication has a broader scope, connecting different types of things with networks, applications and cloud infrastructure. 2. Protocols M2M: Uses mainly non-IP protocols within the local M2M area network. Examples: ZigBee Bluetooth Modbus M-Bus PLC IEEE 802.15.4

SDN – Software-Defined Networking SDN is a networking architecture that separates the control plane from the data plane. It uses a centralized network controller to manage the network. It makes the network simpler, programmable, scalable, and easier to manage. 2. NFV – Network Function Virtualization NFV uses virtualization to convert network functions into software. Functions such as routing, switching, firewalling, and load balancing can run as software. It allows network functions to run on standard servers, switches, and storage instead of specialized hardware. 3. NETCONF – Network Configuration Protocol NETCONF is a network management protocol used to manage network devices. It can retrieve and modify configuration data and retrieve the device's state information. NETCONF is session-based and uses SSH as its transport protocol in the PPT. 4. YANG – Yet Another Next Generation YANG is a data modeling language used with NETCONF. It models configuration data and state data of network devices. YANG organizes data into a hierarchical tree structure using elements such as leaf, container, and list. 5. SNMP – Simple Network Management Protocol SNMP is a network management protocol used to monitor and configure network devices. It can manage devices such as routers, switches, servers, and printers. SNMP uses UDP as its transport protocol and includes components such as NMS, managed device, MIB, and SNMP agent. NETCONF – Network Configuration Protocol NETCONF stands for Network Configuration Protocol. It is a session-based network management protocol used to retrieve and modify configuration data and retrieve the state information of network devices. 1. NETCONF – Network Configuration Protocol NETCONF stands for Network Configuration Protocol. It is a session-based network management protocol used to retrieve and modify configuration data and retrieve the state information of network devices. 1. Why NETCONF is needed Traditional network management using SNMP has some limitations. For example, SNMP is mainly useful for monitoring, and retrieving and restoring complete configurations can be difficult. NETCONF addresses these limitations by allowing administrators to: Retrieve configuration data Modify configuration data Retrieve state/operational data Configure network devices Perform configuration operations reliably 2. How NETCONF works The basic communication is: Management System / Client │ │ NETCONF messages ↓ SSH / TLS │ ↓ NETCONF Server │ ↓ Network Device The client establishes a NETCONF session with the server. After the session is established, they exchange information about their capabilities. The client can then send multiple requests to retrieve or edit configuration data. 3. NETCONF uses SSH According to your PPT: NETCONF works over the SSH transport protocol. The transport layer provides end-to-end connectivity and reliable delivery of messages. NETCONF can also depend on transport protocols such as SSH or TLS for authentication, data integrity, and confidentiality. So remember: NETCONF + SSH → Secure communication with network devices 4. NETCONF uses RPC NETCONF uses XML-encoded Remote Procedure Calls (RPCs) for request and response messages. For example: Client │ │ RPC Request ↓ Server │ │ RPC Response ↓ Client The RPC layer provides a mechanism for encoding RPC calls and notifications. 5. NETCONF Content Layer The Content Layer contains: Configuration data State/operational data This information is XML-encoded. The schema of this configuration and state data is defined using the YANG data modeling language. Simple relationship: NETCONF → Transfers/manages the data YANG → Defines/models the structure of the data 6. NETCONF Configuration Datastore The configuration data is stored in a NETCONF configuration datastore on the server. You can think of it like: NETCONF Server │ ├── Configuration Data │ └── State Data The client can retrieve or modify the configuration data through NETCONF operations. 7. NETCONF Operations NETCONF provides different operations for retrieving and editing configuration data. The important idea is: Retrieve The client can request configuration/state information from the device. Edit The client can modify the configuration of the device. This makes

NETCONF Operations NETCONF provides different operations for retrieving and editing configuration data. The important idea is: Retrieve The client can request configuration/state information from the device. Edit The client can modify the configuration of the device. This makes NETCONF useful not only for monitoring, but also for actual device configuration. 8. NETCONF Session NETCONF is a connection-oriented/session-based protocol. The process is: Step 1 The client establishes a NETCONF session with the server. Step 2 Client and server exchange their capabilities. Step 3 The client sends requests. Step 4 The server processes the requests. Step 5 The server sends responses. The following are five important features: 1. Simple and Easy to Learn Python has a simple and readable syntax. Its syntax is similar to the English language. Therefore, beginners can learn and write Python programs easily. 2. Interpreted Language Python is an interpreted programming language. The program is executed line by line by the Python interpreter. This makes testing and debugging programs easier. 3. Object-Oriented Python supports object-oriented programming (OOP). It supports concepts such as classes, objects, inheritance, and polymorphism. This helps in developing large and reusable programs. 4. Portable Python is a portable language. A Python program written on one operating system can generally run on other operating systems with little or no modification. It supports platforms such as Windows, Linux, and macOS. 5. Large Library Support Python provides a large collection of built-in modules and libraries. These libraries can be used for tasks such as mathematics, file handling, networking, data analysis, and web development. This reduces the amount of code a programmer needs to write. Looping Statements Loops are used to execute a block of code repeatedly. a) for loop A for loop is used to iterate over a sequence such as a list, string, or range. for i in range(1, 6): print(i) Output: 1 2 3 4 5 b) while loop A while loop repeatedly executes a block as long as the condition is True. i = 1 while i <= 5: print(i) i = i + 1 Output: 1 2 3 4 5 3. Jump Statements Jump statements are used to change the normal flow of execution. a) break break is used to immediately stop a loop. for i in range(1, 6): if i == 3: break print(i) Output: 1 2 b) continue continue skips the current iteration and moves to the next iteration. for i in range(1, 6): if i == 3: continue print(i) Output: 1 2 4 5 c) pass pass does nothing.
